docs.title: Blender 5.1 NPR Port - Features and Usage Guide
Project Introduction
docs.text:
Blender 5.1 NPR Port is an NPR-focused Blender branch. In addition to integrating characteristic nodes from Goo Engine and the 4.4 NPR-prototype, it adds a set of Eevee-oriented extension nodes, filter workflows, and interface improvements.

Most features are Eevee-only and do not support Cycles.

docs.title: Documentation Scope
docs.text: This document describes the NPR / Eevee extension features that have been added to the current Blender 5.1 NPR Port branch compared with official Blender 5.1, together with their basic usage.

All NPR Port features require the Eevee render engine. Cycles is not supported.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
Add > Input > Filter Object Info

Available only in the Filter domain.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads the world-space transform and viewport display color of a chosen object, making it easier to drive full-screen filters from scene helpers or controller objects.

docs.title: Node Setting
docs.text: • Object

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Location
  • Rotation
  • Scale
  • Color

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Location: world-space location of the chosen object
  • Rotation: world-space Euler rotation in radians
  • Scale: world-space scale of the chosen object
  • Color: viewport display color of the chosen object
  • If no object is assigned, the node falls back to 0 for location / rotation / color and 1 for scale

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
Add > Input > Filter Mask

Available only in the Filter domain.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Uses Eevee Cryptomatte object information to build fast object masks for filter materials.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: • Mask

docs.title: Panel Options
docs.text:
• Mode
  • Single Object
  • Object List
  • Collection

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Single Object is useful for one controller object
  • Object List is useful when a manual object set is needed, and can be filled from the current selection
  • Collection is useful when the mask should follow a collection hierarchy
  • The output is a 0-1 float mask that can be used with Mix, thresholds, AOV writing, or any other filter logic
  • Only renderable geometry objects are supported

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
Add > Input > Scene Color

Available only in the Filter domain.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Reads the current Eevee scene buffer. The Source can be switched in the node panel:

  • Color
  • Depth
  • Normal
  • Position

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Input: Vector
  • Outputs: Color, Alpha

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Color: read the resolved scene color
  • Depth: read linear scene depth
  • Normal: read scene normals
  • Position: read the world-space position pass
  • If Vector is not connected, the node samples with the Window output of the Texture Coordinate node

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Render Info

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Frag Coord
  • Width
  • Height

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provides the coordinate and pixel size of the current Eevee render window.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Frag Coord.xy is normalized screen UV in 0-1
  • Frag Coord.z is the current fragment depth
  • Width / Height are the current render-region pixel dimensions

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Scene Time

docs.title: Input
docs.text: • Scale

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Frame
  • Seconds
  • Timeline
  • Scaled Frame

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Provides time-related values from the current scene.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > Math > Screen Derivative

docs.title: Feature
docs.text:
Gets the difference between neighboring pixels in screen space:

  • DDX
  • DDY
  • DDXY

where DDXY means DDX + DDY.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
• Add > Layout > Portal In
  • Add > Layout > Portal Out

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text: These are “portal” nodes used to organize node links.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Portal In: stores a named, typed value in the current node tree
  • Portal Out: retrieves that value later by name inside the same node tree
  • Creating a new Portal In generates a unique name automatically
  • Portal Out includes a magnifier button that jumps to the matching Portal In
  • Portals are only recognized inside the same shader node tree and do not automatically pass through node groups

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Texture > Render Texture

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads a Render Textures entry configured in the scene.

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Input: Vector
  • Outputs: Color, Alpha

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Screenspace Info

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Input: View Position
  • Outputs: Scene Color, Scene Depth

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads color or depth from the current render buffer.

docs.title: Usage Notes
docs.text:
• Raytracing must be enabled in render settings
  • Material Render Method must be set to Dithered
  • Raytraced Transmission must be enabled
  • The default View Position input transforms the current position into camera space and then flips the Z axis

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > World Environment

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Input: Direction
  • Output: Color

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Directly samples the Eevee world environment color without depending on whether geometry exists behind the screen.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• If Direction is not connected, the current surface view direction is used
  • If Direction is connected, the world environment is sampled in that direction
  • The result is closer to Eevee environment / probe lighting than to a screen-space buffer

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Light Probe Color

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Input: Direction
  • Outputs: Reflection, Irradiance, Combined

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads the currently available Eevee lighting-probe result directly, splitting it into reflection, irradiance, and combined outputs.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > Vector > World To Tangent

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Input: Vector
  • Output: Vector

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Converts a world-space direction vector into the tangent space of the current surface.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A UV Map can be chosen in the node panel, and the tangent of that UV is used as the basis
  • This is useful for anisotropic direction control, tangent-space flow, and local scan-direction effects

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
Add > Script > GLSL Function

Available in both Eevee object materials and NPR Tree.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Injects a user-authored GLSL function into the current Eevee / NPR material compile path.

docs.title: Supported Boundary Types
docs.text:
• Input parameters: float, vec2, vec3, vec4, sampler2D, sample2D
  • Output parameters: out float, out vec2, out vec3, out vec4
  • Return values: void, float, vec2, vec3, vec4

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Function is not auto-selected and must be chosen explicitly
  • sampler2D uses image slots in the node panel instead of link sockets
  • sample2D becomes a Closure input and can be driven by Image to Closure or a compatible Closure Output
  • Closure Output -> sample2D currently guarantees only the direct texture(tex, uv) form
  • @glsl_meta supports default, min, max, hide_value, and subtype
  • Only vec3 / vec4 inputs explicitly marked with subtype=color become color sockets

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
Add > Texture > Image to Closure

Available in both Eevee object materials and NPR Tree.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: • Closure

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Wraps a regular image as a closure-backed source for sample2D workflows.

docs.title: Node Settings
docs.text:
• Image
  • Interpolation
  • Extension

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > Vector > Basis Transform

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Uses Origin + three basis axes to perform custom coordinate-space transforms inside material nodes.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > Vector > Twirl

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Inputs: Vector, Center, Amount
  • Output: Vector

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Twists the input coordinate field around a chosen center. This is useful for Goo Engine style swirls, distorted UVs, and radial deformations.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Texture > Water Ripples

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Inputs: Vector, Time, Scale, Intensity, Speed, Detail, Bias
  • Outputs: Distorted Vector, Mask

docs.title: Panel Options
docs.text:
• Mode
  • Drops
  • Ripples
  • Flow
  • Caustic

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Generates procedural ripple distortion and a ripple mask.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Texture > Hex Grid Texture

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Vector
  • Scale
  • Size
  • Radius
  • Roundness

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Value
  • Color
  • Hex Coords
  • Position
  • Cell UV
  • Cell ID

docs.title: Panel Options
docs.text:
• Coordinate Mode
  • XY Position
  • Hex Position
  • Value Mode
  • Hexagons
  • SDF Hexagons
  • Dots
  • Direction
  • Horizontal
  • Vertical
  • Horizontal Tiled
  • Vertical Tiled
  • Clamp

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Generates a hex-grid texture that can be used for honeycomb patterns, cell partitioning, SDF masks, and hex-coordinate based lookups.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Texture > SDF Primitive

docs.title: Output
docs.text: • Distance

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Generates signed-distance-field base shapes directly inside material nodes.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Converter > SDF Operator

docs.title: Output
docs.text: • Distance

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Combines, trims, and reshapes one or two SDF distance fields.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > Vector > SDF Vector Operator

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Vector
  • Position
  • Value

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Preprocesses coordinate, UV, or vector domains before they are fed into SDF Primitive.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Bevel

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Inputs: Radius, Normal
  • Output: Normal

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Generates an approximate beveled normal in Eevee so hard edges can look smoother.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Curvature

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• Samples
  • Sample Radius
  • Thickness
  • Scale

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Scene Curvature
  • Scene Rim

docs.title: Panel Options
docs.text:
• Local
  • Sample Radius
  • Pixel
  • View

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• In Pixel mode, Sample Radius is interpreted in pixels and therefore changes with render resolution
  • In View mode, Sample Radius is interpreted relative to the view, which helps keep rim width more consistent between viewport and final render
  • This is still a screen-space node, so the result depends on camera view, resolution, and sampling radius

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Shader Info

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
• World Position
  • Normal
  • Exponent

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Diffuse Shading
  • Shadow
  • Ambient Lighting
  • Half-Lambert Factor
  • Blinn-Phong Factor

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Shadow Mode
  • Built-in
  • Soft Filtered
  • Blinn-Phong Factor outputs a Blinn-Phong highlight factor weighted by the light specular channel
  • The node panel includes a Lightgroup control

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Input > Light Info

docs.title: Fixed Outputs
docs.text:
• Color
  • Power
  • Type

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Type is an integer socket
  • For per-light processing, use For Each Light in the NPR Tree

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Converter > Color Ramp

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Color Ramp now supports an OKLab blend mode, giving more stable and perceptually smoother color transitions.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The old standalone OKLab Color Ramp node has been merged back into Color Ramp
  • Existing node setups should now use the OKLab mode on Color Ramp directly

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Shows Eevee viewport / final-render performance statistics, stage breakdowns, and hints directly in the Outliner, making it easier to locate heavy parts of the pipeline.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
• Outliner > Display Mode > Eevee Performance
  • Profiler / Pause / Sort by Time in the Outliner header
  • The Eevee Performance popover in the Outliner header

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Enabling Profiler starts collecting performance statistics and displays them in the Outliner
  • Pause freezes live updates so the current result can be inspected
  • Sort by Time sorts the stage list by CPU cost instead of fixed pipeline order
  • Average Window sets the frame window used for smoothing statistics
  • The tree currently includes groups such as Viewport, Final Render, Metadata, Features, Stages, and Hints

docs.title: Current Scope
docs.text:
• This is mainly a CPU-side Eevee stage profiler and hint view, not a full GPU profiler
  • It is meaningful only for Eevee, not for Cycles

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Controls whether material previews are rendered in material drop-downs and search lists.

This is mainly useful when many materials exist and expanding the selector would otherwise trigger too many preview renders.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Edit > Preferences > Editing > Objects > Materials > Material Selector Previews

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• When enabled: the selector shows material previews as usual
  • When disabled: the selector falls back to normal material icons and no longer triggers preview renders in the drop-down list
  • Default value: enabled

docs.title: Current Scope
docs.text:
• Only affects template_ID(...) style material pickers in drop-down lists
  • Does not affect the large preview sphere in Material Properties
  • Does not affect the actual material render result

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Adds clearer face-culling control for materials. In addition to the usual back-face culling, the NPR Port also supports Front culling.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Material Properties > Settings > Culling > Camera

docs.title: Available Modes
docs.text:
• None: render both front and back faces
  • Back: hide back-facing faces
  • Front: hide front-facing faces

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Front is useful for shell-style effects, inside-view setups, or some inverted-outline style tricks
  • Shadow and Light Probe Volume still keep their own culling controls

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Assigns an integer light-group ID to Eevee lights so the Shader Info node can filter direct-light evaluation by group.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Light Data > Light > Lightgroup ID

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Default value: 0
  • When Shader Info also uses Lightgroup = 0, only lights with Lightgroup ID = 0 are evaluated
  • If a Shader Info node uses another integer value, only lights with the same ID are included
  • This grouping currently affects only Shader Info, not the default Eevee material lighting path

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Adds a dedicated Outliner visibility flag to each Pose Bone, making it easier to organize complex rigs without changing rig behavior itself.

docs.title: Entry
docs.text:
• Bone Properties > Viewport Display > Hide in Outliner
  • Outliner > Filter > Hidden PoseBones

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Every Pose Bone has its own Hide in Outliner toggle
  • The toggle is enabled by default
  • The Hidden PoseBones filter in the Outliner is also enabled by default, so existing rigs do not immediately change appearance
  • After disabling Outliner > Filter > Hidden PoseBones, bones with Hide in Outliner enabled are hidden from the tree
  • If a hidden parent still has visible child bones, those visible children remain in the tree instead of removing the whole hierarchy

docs.title: Current Scope
docs.text:
• Affects Pose Bone only
  • Does not affect Edit Bone
  • Changes only the Outliner hierarchy display, not transforms, animation, drivers, or rendering

docs.title: 1. Basic Concept
docs.text:
NPR Tree is a second shading graph attached to a regular object material. It is used to reorganize and stylize Eevee material results in an NPR-oriented way.

The regular object material still handles the base surface shading, while the NPR Tree adds an extra NPR presentation layer on top.

docs.title: 2. How to Attach It
docs.text:
1. Keep the normal Material Output and base shading in the regular object material.
  2. Select the Material Output node.
  3. Create or assign a node group in its NPR Tree property.
  1. To edit this tree, switch the Shader Editor top Shader Type to NPR.

docs.title: 3. Notes
docs.text:
• The material render mode needs to be set to Dithered (Deferred)
  • Ctrl + Tab can be used to switch quickly between the regular object material and the NPR tree
  • NPR Tree keyframes and drivers use a dedicated NPR Tree Action, which can be viewed, switched, or created in Material Properties > Animation > NPR Tree Action

docs.title: 4. Main NPR Nodes
docs.text: In addition to the dedicated NPR nodes below, Curvature, Raycast, and GLSL Function can also be used directly inside NPR Tree.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads the input buffers provided by the NPR rendering stage.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Combined Color
  • Diffuse Color
  • Diffuse Direct
  • Diffuse Indirect
  • Specular Color
  • Specular Direct
  • Specular Indirect
  • Position
  • Normal

These outputs are closer to image / texture handles than ordinary scalar values, so they are typically passed to Image Sample or other NPR-aware nodes for further processing.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads refraction-related buffers, similar in spirit to Screenspace Info.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Combined Color
  • Position

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > Image Sample

docs.title: Inputs / Outputs
docs.text:
• Inputs: Image, Offset
  • Output: Color

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Samples image-style handles such as those coming from NPR Input or NPR Refraction.

docs.title: Offset Modes
docs.text:
• View: offset in view space
  • Pixel: offset in pixel space

docs.title: Entry
docs.text: Add > Utilities > For Each Light

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: This node runs its internal logic once for every light affecting the current surface and outputs per-light information during each iteration.

docs.title: Built-In Data
docs.text:
For Each Light Input currently provides:

  • Input: Normal
  • Outputs: Color, Direction, Distance, Attenuation, Shadow Mask

It also supports custom area input / output sockets so intermediate values can be passed through the per-light loop.

docs.title: 5. Built-In NPR Node Group Assets
docs.text: This version already ports a group of commonly used node groups from the Blender 4.4 NPR branch and repackages them as 5.1-compatible assets.

docs.title: Main Built-In Assets
docs.text:
• Cavity
  • Co-Planar Edge Detection
  • Curvature
  • Kuwahara
  • Shading Models
  • Surface Curvature

docs.title: Asset Notes
docs.text:
• These node groups have been migrated to the Blender 5.1 format
  • Because repeat-zone node names changed, old Blender 4.4 NPR Prototype files may need to reconnect region-related nodes manually

Eevee Only

NPR Tree currently supports only Eevee, not Cycles.

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text:
Render Textures is an additional scene-level Eevee render-texture system.

It lets a scene maintain up to 4 render texture slots. Each slot can point to a camera and an output type, rendering that camera view into a texture that can later be sampled by the Render Texture node in regular object materials.

docs.title: Panel Entry
docs.text: Scene Properties > Render Textures

docs.title: Configurable Fields
docs.text:
Each Render Texture entry currently supports:

  • Name
  • Enabled
  • Source
  • Color: Capture the final Eevee color
  • Depth: Capture linear depth
  • Normal: Capture normals
  • Camera
  • Resolution X / Y
  • Update Mode
  • Every Sample
  • Every Frame
  • Manual
  • Format
  • RGBA16F
  • RGBA32F
  • R16F
  • R32F

docs.title: Basic Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open Scene Properties > Render Textures.
  2. Create a new Render Texture entry.
  3. Choose Source, Camera, resolution, update mode, and format.
  4. Add a Add > Texture > Render Texture node in a regular object material.
  5. Pick the matching Render Texture entry in the node panel.
  6. Use the node's Color / Alpha outputs in the rest of the material.

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text: Filter Materials is a scene-level Eevee full-screen filter stack. Each entry is a material in the Filter domain, and the stack is applied in list order to the current frame.

docs.title: Panel Entry
docs.text:
Scene Properties > Filter Materials

Node-tree entry: Shader Editor > Shader Type > Filter

docs.title: Basic Workflow
docs.text:
1. Open Scene Properties > Filter Materials.
  2. Create a new entry, or click New Filter Material.
  3. The selected material must be a Filter domain material.
  4. In the Shader Editor, switch the top Shader Type to Filter.
  5. Use Scene Color to read scene data, and combine it with Filter Object Info or Filter Mask when object-driven control is needed.
  6. Use AOV Input if the filter needs to read an existing custom pass.
  7. Use AOV Output if the filter should write an intermediate or final result into a named AOV.
  8. Choose the insertion point with Execution Stage.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• The default sampling coordinate for Scene Color is the Window output of the Texture Coordinate node
  • AOV Input is supported
  • AOV Output is supported, so a filter can write to a named AOV before sending the final result into Filter Output
  • Execution Stage currently provides three insertion points:
  • Before Volume Fog
  • Before Depth of Field
  • Before Composite
